biography: Gregorio Bertocco wasn't born into a racing dynasty. His family owned a small vineyard in the Veneto region of Italy, where Gregorio spent his childhood surrounded by rolling hills and the scent of grapes. His passion for speed ignited when a local karting track opened nearby. He spent every spare moment there, saving his allowance to rent karts and hone his skills. His natural talent was undeniable, attracting the attention of a regional racing team. His big break came at the Italian GT Championship, where he placed second, catching the eye of Ligier. Now at 30, Bertocco is considered to be at his peak and is a consistent contender, carefully plotting his next move to climb higher in the racing world. He remains fiercely proud of his humble origins, often returning to the vineyard to clear his head before crucial races.
drivingStyle: Bertocco's driving style is best described as calculating aggression. He meticulously analyzes every corner, optimizing his entry and exit speeds with laser-like precision. Unlike some drivers who rely on raw instinct, Bertocco prefers a more methodical approach, studying telemetry data and identifying subtle advantages. He is known for his exceptional tire management, conserving rubber early in the race to unleash blistering pace in the final laps. While not afraid to make bold moves, he always prioritizes risk assessment, ensuring that every maneuver is carefully calculated for maximum gain and minimal risk.

careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the Ligier JS2 R after a tense final hour where he managed to overtake his rival with only 10 minutes to spare.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Monza Grand Prix after a mechanical failure, costing him a home victory and significant championship points.
